title: Belonging is becoming a practical test of whether everyday systems, places and institutions feel workable and fair
geography: United Kingdom adults aged 18 and over; nationally and politically representative weighted survey across all four nations

observations.period: December 1-17, 2025; third wave of the UK Belonging Barometer

denominator.unit: UK adults aged 18 and over surveyed by Opinium

framework.value: belonging is measured across People, Place, Power and Purpose: relationships, shared environments, influence over decisions, and meaning or contribution

belonging.value: 73% say they belong at least somewhat, while 22% say they do not really belong or do not belong at all

measurement_use.value: the Barometer is designed to track connection, inclusion, voice and contribution over time and to inform policy and community practice

observations.method: Opinium survey conducted 1-17 December 2025 with 10,001 UK adults; results weighted to be nationally and politically representative across all four nations.
observations.uncertainty: The findings are self-reported associations and perceptions from one survey wave; they do not establish causal effects of housing, services, politics or relationships on belonging.
observations.subgroup: UK adults across age, health, disability, housing, relationship, sexuality, faith, work and regional groups.
observations.counterinterpretation: A multidimensional belonging measure can reveal system strain that loneliness measures miss, but it still cannot determine which intervention would produce durable connection or whether reported belonging changes behavior.

observations.period: Since 2020; reported change in national and local connection

denominator.unit: UK adult belonging comparison with the start of the 2020s

national_connection.value: 39% feel less connected to modern Britain than at the start of the decade, compared with 14% who feel more connected

local_resilience.value: local connection appears more stable: 22% feel more connected to their local community, 24% less connected and 48% report no change

community_infrastructure.value: 27% report fewer opportunities to meet new people, 26% a lower sense of community and 33% less confidence in local decision-making

observations.method: Retrospective survey comparison of perceived connection, community opportunities, local pride and local decision-making since 2020.
observations.uncertainty: Retrospective perceptions may reflect recall, changing reference points and contemporaneous economic or political conditions; the result is not a longitudinal individual panel.
observations.subgroup: UK adults with different local, regional and national attachments, including people with and without disabilities.
observations.counterinterpretation: National disconnection can coexist with resilient local ties, and reported local stability does not prove that local institutions, services or social networks are functioning equally well everywhere.

observations.period: 2025; economic, time and local-service pressures on participation

denominator.unit: UK adults surveyed in the Belonging Barometer

economic_pressure.value: 86% say at least one economic factor has made it harder to build connections, and 58% say the rising cost of living limits their ability to take part in community life

local_change.value: 74% say their local area has changed since the pandemic; 37% report changes to local businesses or high streets and 34% changes to local services such as GP surgeries, schools or public transport

life_stage_pressure.value: adults aged 35-54 report weaker connection and life satisfaction alongside caring responsibilities, financial strain and time scarcity

observations.method: Survey questions on economic barriers, local change, participation, time pressure and life-stage differences, interpreted through the People, Place, Power and Purpose framework.
observations.uncertainty: The report identifies linked pressures rather than isolating their causal contribution; local changes and economic barriers may be experienced differently across regions and groups.
observations.subgroup: Midlife adults, renters, unemployed people, people with caring responsibilities, people facing high travel or housing costs and residents dependent on local services.
observations.counterinterpretation: Economic pressure may reduce some forms of participation while redirecting people toward lower-cost relationships, mutual aid, online spaces or informal community activity that the survey may not fully capture.

observations.period: 2025; unequal belonging across health, housing, age and identity

denominator.unit: UK adults surveyed, with subgroup comparisons

health.value: poor physical and especially mental health are consistently linked to weaker friendship satisfaction, life meaning and overall belonging

security.value: homeowners, married people and retirees report stronger neighbourhood connection and life satisfaction, while renters, unemployed people and separated or divorced people report weaker connection

identity_and_representation.value: young adults report social activity alongside anxiety, loneliness and weaker life satisfaction; LGBT+ respondents report weaker belonging, neighbourhood connection and political trust; people with disabilities report greater disconnection and weaker representation

observations.method: Cross-sectional demographic and wellbeing comparisons across the Barometer's four belonging dimensions.
observations.uncertainty: Subgroup differences are descriptive associations and may reflect intersecting health, income, housing, discrimination, age, relationship and accessibility conditions that are not fully separated in the report.
observations.subgroup: Young adults, midlife adults, renters, unemployed people, LGBT+ people, people with disabilities, people in poor health and people with weaker housing or relationship security.
observations.counterinterpretation: Stronger belonging among more secure groups may reflect selection, life stage or existing resources rather than housing tenure or relationship status directly causing connection.

related_sources.claim: Belonging Forum publication page with headline findings, the People-Place-Power-Purpose framework and related constituency and disability reports.
Prior Belonging Barometer wave for the publication's repeated-measurement context.

boundary: This record adds a UK belonging, place, participation and institutional-performance layer linking social connection to relationships, local spaces, housing, services, economic pressure, time, health and political representation. It is a nationally weighted cross-sectional survey and descriptive trend comparison, not a longitudinal panel, causal evaluation, behavioral observation or proof that any single factor produces belonging.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official Belonging Forum publication page and 34-page 2026 PDF were reviewed for the 10,001-person methodology, People-Place-Power-Purpose framework, belonging levels, since-2020 connection change, economic and local-service pressures, and subgroup patterns.
